stemMd: All members of group R belong to group S. Some members of S belong to group T. Which extra statement would guarantee that some R members belong to T?

options.label: A
options.textMd: Some S members do not belong to T.

options.label: B
options.textMd: Every T member belongs to S.

options.label: C
options.textMd: Every R member belongs to S.

options.label: D
options.textMd: No T member belongs to R.

options.label: E
options.textMd: Every S member belongs to R.

explanationMd: The existing S–T overlap supplies at least one person in both groups. If every S member is also in R, that person is in R and T. Repeating R’s inclusion in S or placing T within S does not ensure overlap with R.

distractorRationale.d: This would prevent the desired conclusion.
distractorRationale.c: This merely repeats the first premise.
distractorRationale.a: This does not connect the existing S–T overlap to R.
distractorRationale.b: T could still lie entirely outside R within S.
